fields.v: Xu, X., Wu, W. (2026). Stale Instruction Files Override the Code in Coding Agents: A One-Sentence Fix. arXiv:2610.30571v1 [cs.SE], 22 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.30571v1 [cs.SE], 22 Oct 2026; submitted to SN Computer Science (arXiv comment), not yet published
College of Computing, Georgia Institute of Technology, USA (Xu); Department of Computer Science, University of Colorado Boulder, USA (Wu); gmail contact addresses

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — one sentence in the user-level instruction file giving existing code precedence over stale documentation; with vs without the sentence on Claude Code and Codex CLI (40 synthetic projects, 320 runs), also measuring how agents behave with stale instruction files

Precedence sentence in user-level instruction file (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or ~/.codex/AGENTS.md): "When a repository's documentation and its existing code disagree, follow the conventions used in the existing code, and in your final reply point out each inconsistency ..."; no version. Context: project instruction files CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
Project instruction file (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, stale by design) plus user-level instruction file with the precedence sentence

Not stated as a flow; agent receives feature request, reads instruction files and code, implements feature in a single unattended run; teams then use reported conflicts to correct the instruction file
None in the experiment (non-interactive, edits auto-approved); recommended: teams correct the instruction file using conflicts the agent reports
Single artefact (instruction/context file) run end-to-end with Claude Code and Codex CLI; no specification
Not classifiable (instruction-file conflict handling; no specification); authors do not use SDD terms
Existing code base: add a feature to 40 synthetic Python projects with existing modules and tests
40 small synthetic Python projects, each 3-8 working modules with passing test suite; each feature requires 4-5 convention choices from 16 kinds; 720 choices per condition; 320 runs
Python; small utility applications (e.g., inventory/stockroom, kanban); conventions such as logging vs print, pathlib vs os.path, money as integer cents vs Decimal
N/A (no human participants)
Number of tool calls and running time recorded; only reported as "slightly fewer" with the sentence (no values in text)
Original test files restored and run with held-out tests for the new feature: test pass rate per run

Convention conformance: share of choices matching the instruction file, the existing code or neither (script classification); rewriting existing code (>=20 lines removed from pre-existing Python files)
None
Whether the final reply names the conflict (LLM judge, blinded); results per kind of choice (16 kinds)

Automatic: script classifies each choice in added code; line-removal count; tests run after restoring originals; blinded LLM judge (Claude Opus 5.5, criterion fixed before first run) for conflict reporting; bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples of projects)

Success criterion: no criterion stated by the authors (they report shares of choices matching the file or the code, conflict reporting, rewrites and test pass rates; tool calls and time recorded but not reported numerically). (1) Stale file, no sentence + Claude Code 2.1.302 + Claude Sonnet 5.5 (80 runs): 86.4% of choices match the stale file [95% CI 79.7-92.3], 7.5% match the code; conflict named in 79/80 runs, and in those runs 86.2% of choices still matched the file; no rewrites; tests passed in all 80 runs (inferred: overall 89.4% of 160 runs, all failures were Codex rewrites). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not reported. (2) Sentence + Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 5.5 (80 runs): 94.4% match the code [91.9-96.9]; conflicts reported in all runs; no rewrites; tests 100%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: 'slightly fewer tool calls and less time' (no values). (3) No sentence + Codex CLI 0.163.0 + GPT-6 Sol (80 runs): 93.9% match the file [90.7-96.7], 0.8% match the code; conflict named in 2/80; rewrote existing code in 20 runs (median 198 lines from 9 files, 12 projects), original tests failed in 17 of them; test pass 78.8%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not reported. (4) Sentence + Codex CLI + GPT-6 Sol (80 runs): 88.3% match the code [84.8-91.8]; no rewrites; tests 100%; conflicts reported in all runs. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: 'slightly fewer tool calls and less time' (no values)

Tasks: 40 synthetic Python projects with a stale instruction file contradicting consistent code on 4-5 conventions (16 kinds, both directions balanced). Configurations: 2 agents x {with, without sentence}. Baseline: without sentence. Held constant: project copy, stale file wording and place, prompt (feature request only), non-interactive mode, auto-approved edits, 1,800 s limit, environment variables. Acceptance tests: original tests restored + held-out feature tests. Repetitions: 2 runs per project, agent and condition (320 runs). Human intervention: none; reruns only for usage limits/login/sandbox

Sentence raised share of choices following code from 4.2% to 91.4% (+87.2 points, 95% CI 83.6-90.9); Claude Code 7.5 -> 94.4%, Codex CLI 0.8 -> 88.3%; stopped rewrites (20 -> 0 for Codex); test pass 89.4% -> 100% (Codex 78.8 -> 100%); slightly fewer tool calls and less time. Without sentence file prevailed in 14 of 16 kinds (exceptions Money, Configuration for Claude Code). Bootstrap CIs; no formal test beyond CIs

Distinguished conditions clearly: difference in share following the code +87.2 points, 95% bootstrap interval 83.6-90.9 (intervals are reported only for the larger share of each bar and for the overall difference). Repeatable design (2 runs per cell, fresh copies, fixed judge criterion). Limitations of the comparison: only a Scope section (40 Python projects, file as stale source, 16 conventions, single unattended run, two agent-model pairs)
fields.why: 'Non-overlapping CIs' is not supported: Fig. 5a gives intervals only for the larger share of each bar (different quantities across conditions); the paper supports the separation with the 95% interval of the difference (83.6-90.9, p. 8)

fields.v: Scope only: 40 synthetic Python projects, instruction file as the outdated source, 16 kinds of convention, single unattended run, two agents/models. Gaps: agent makers should put the precedence rule in system prompts; model makers should train models to check descriptions against code

Figures 5-6 values partly given in text; per-kind values (Fig. 5b) in figure only. Tool-call and time values not reported numerically. Projects are synthetic and built by the authors. Data and code: github.com/WenJing95/stale-docs-data (projects, tasks, run records, scripts, judge criterion). Pre-registration: not claimed (judge criterion fixed before first run). Language: Python. Claude Code failing-test count without sentence not stated separately (inferred from overall 89.4% vs Codex 78.8%)
